sources.entry: Claude Code Infrastructure Showcase by diet103 - A remarkably innovative approach to working with Skills, the centerpiece of which being a technique that leverages hooks to ensure that Claude intelligently selects and activates the appropriate Skill given the current context. Well-documented and adaptable to different projects and workflows.

summary.one_liner: A reference library of Claude Code infrastructure (hooks, skills, agents, slash commands) that auto-suggests skills based on prompts and file context, meant to be copied into your own projects rather than run as an application.
summary.what_it_does: The repo provides a .claude/ directory with four skills (backend-dev-guidelines, frontend-dev-guidelines, skill-developer, error-tracking), nine hooks, eight agents, and slash commands. A UserPromptSubmit hook checks skill-rules.json against each prompt and file context to suggest relevant skills, and PreToolUse and PostToolUse hooks enforce or track skill activation before and after edits. Skill activation runs in a regex-only mode by default, with an optional AI classification mode (Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, or Ollama) that falls back to regex. The README also describes a modular skill layout (a main SKILL.md under 500 lines plus resource files) and a dev docs pattern with plan, context, and tasks files to survive context resets. A setup wizard (setup.ts) copies the files into a target project, detects the tech stack, and runs health checks; a verify-setup script checks the install. The README also describes a Codex CLI adapter that reuses the same hooks.
use_cases: Make Claude Code suggest the right skill automatically based on prompts
Enforce skill loading before Claude edits files
Share coding conventions as modular skills with progressive disclosure
Preserve project context across Claude Code context resets with dev docs
Set up Claude Code hooks, agents, and slash commands in an existing project
Use regex or AI-based intent matching to route prompts to skills
notable: Hook-based skill auto-activation driven by skill-rules.json, so skills suggest themselves instead of being invoked manually
Optional PreToolUse guard that blocks edits until mandatory skills are activated, with a two-try model
Three activation modes (disabled, fallback, ai-only) with regex as a graceful fallback when AI is unavailable
Setup wizard that copies files, detects the stack, and runs self-verification checks
Modular skill pattern: main SKILL.md under 500 lines plus resource files loaded on demand
caveats: Hooks are bash scripts; macOS, Linux, or WSL2 only, not plain cmd or PowerShell
Reference library, not a working application; examples use a generic blog domain and some hooks need customization for your project layout
Optional Stop hooks such as tsc-check are described as heavy and suited to monorepos only
